titleEn: Mahāmṛtyuñjaya asks Śiva: let me fall from death's grip like a ripe cucumber from its stem.
sanskrit: ॐ त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् । उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान् मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात् ॥
transliteration: oṃ tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭi-vardhanam · urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya mā'mṛtāt
meaningEn: We worship the three-eyed one — fragrant, the one who makes all that lives grow strong. As a ripe cucumber drops from its stem on its own, may I be freed from the grip of death — but not from the deathless. The picture is the whole teaching: not torn away, but ripe and released.
meaningHi: हम तीन आँखों वाले शिव की पूजा करते हैं — जो सुगंध हैं, जो सबको पालते और बढ़ाते हैं। जैसे पका हुआ खीरा बेल से अपने-आप छूट जाता है, वैसे ही मैं मौत की पकड़ से छूट जाऊँ — पर अमृत से नहीं। यही तस्वीर पूरी सीख है: तोड़ा नहीं गया, पका और छूटा।
sayItLike: Om tryam-ba-kam ya-jaa-ma-he · su-gan-dhim push-ti-var-dha-nam · ur-vaa-ru-kam iva ban-dha-naan · mrit-yor muk-shee-ya maa-mri-taat

words.grammar: the one we worship — object of yajāmahe

words.glossEn: we worship, we make offering to

words.grammar: describes the three-eyed one; matching -ṃ ending

words.glossEn: who makes nourishment grow — who feeds all life
words.glossHi: जो सबको पालते और बढ़ाते हैं

words.grammar: the picture of the whole mantra

words.glossEn: from its stem — from what binds it
words.glossHi: बेल से — जो बाँधे रखता है उससे
words.grammar: bandhanāt, 'from the binding' — ablative; -t becomes -n before m (sandhi)
from death — ablative; mṛtyoḥ becomes mṛtyor before a voiced sound
may-I-be-freed — first person, a wish; the only ask in the mantra
'not' — joins the next word: mā + amṛtāt = māmṛtāt

words.glossHi: अमृत से — जो कभी नहीं मरता उससे
words.grammar: from the deathless — ablative; 'freed from death, not from the deathless'

source.ref: 7.59.12; also Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.8.6.2 and Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 3.60
source.note: Ṛgveda 7.59.12 is widely held to be a late addition to its hymn — a question about date, not about the words. The opening oṃ is liturgical and is not part of the Ṛgveda line.

significance.textSays: Ṛgveda 7.59.12: a plea to the three-eyed one to be loosed from death's bond as a cucumber from its stem — and 'not from the deathless' (mā'mṛtāt). The wish is for a ripe, unforced release.
significance.traditionSays: Chanted at Śivarātri, for the sick and for the dying — 108 times, often by a whole family together. Called the great death-conquering mantra.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That it heals, lengthens life or shields from harm. It is a prayer, quoted exactly; what tradition hopes from it is labelled as tradition.

practice.timeOfDay: morning; at Śivarātri; by tradition at a sickbed; Monday's mantra in this app
